'''The Quintarad''' was a [[Star system/Legends|star system]]<ref name="Author's Cut" /> located within [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]],<ref name="EAOC" /> in the otherwise [[Star/Legends|starless]] region known as the [[Void of Aogros/Legends|Void of Aogros]]. The system consisted of five stars [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] each other and was considered an oddity.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

[[Astrophysicist/Legends|Astrophysicists]] were convinced that the Quintarad was artificial by nature, and it was widely believed to have been constructed by members of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Celestial/Legends|Celestial]] [[Species/Legends|species]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> who had disappeared from the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] by [[30,000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Several [[Probe droid/Legends|probes]] were sent into the quinary system, but none of them survived the journey.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Quintarad was originally meant to be mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the sidebar that would have mentioned the star system was cut before the book's release.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The information regarding the Quintarad was later released in [[2013]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Quintarad in grid square H-18.<ref name="EAOC" />
